source: Product copy written FROM THE PHOTOGRAPHS, Sep 2026 — the ten live products that had a word instead of a description.
notes: Dry run first:  GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/key.json npx tsx scripts/import-catalogue.ts docs/ops/fixups/2026-09-descriptions-photographed.json --prod --dry-run
Drop --dry-run to write. Only the fields present here are touched.

Every line describes what is actually in the product's own photograph - colour, cut, fabric, embellishment - not what its name says. Several names describe a different garment than the picture shows; see the mismatches listed in the commit message.
Listing Status and Image URL are deliberately ABSENT. All ten are already Active, and sending Active with no Image URL would make the importer demote them to Draft - taking them off the website.
These ten SUPERSEDE the same ten rows in 2026-09-descriptions.json, which were inferred from product names before the photographs were read.

TC00101 has no main photograph but three real gallery shots, so its copy is written from those. Its name says SAREE; the photographs show a blouse, a drape skirt and a cape — a three-piece set, which is what its category already says.

rows.Description: Marigold yellow, cut as a tiered anarkali that sweeps to the floor. The bodice is embroidered in pastel florals with mirror work catching the light; the skirt is gathered through three soft tiers of georgette. Haldi and mehendi dressing.

Deep violet Banarasi silk, worked all over in gold zari butis, with a wide brocade border running the length of the dupatta. The V-neck blouse is embroidered to match and finished with a row of pearl drops. A wedding piece, meant for the main ceremony.

A light-wash denim playsuit with a collared, long-sleeved shirt top and flap pockets at the chest, nipped in with cut-outs at the waist and finished with a raw frayed hem. Roll the cuffs, add white sneakers, and it is done.

A lehenga choli in iridescent sequinned net — pale rose that shifts through lilac and silver as it turns. The blouse is embroidered in pastel threadwork with a scalloped hem; the dupatta is sheer, edged in blue-green scallops. Reception dressing.

A pre-draped saree in flowing black georgette, so it goes on like a gown and falls like a saree. The high-neck blouse is hand-beaded with a fringe of beadwork over the shoulder, and the waist is finished with an embellished belt. Cocktail and reception wear.

A mother-and-daughter set in slubbed grey chambray, scattered with tiny multicoloured woven dots. Hers falls from a fitted bodice into a full blush-pink skirt; the little one's is a tie-shoulder pinafore cut from the same cloth. Made to be worn together.

A red fit-and-flare midi, sleeveless, with a split notch at the neckline and princess seams shaping the bodice before the skirt opens out to mid-calf. The dress to own when one dress has to cover everything.

Lime yellow in three pieces: a cropped blouse embroidered in white floral threadwork, a softly pleated drape skirt, and a full-length sheer cape with embroidery running down both front edges. The cape does the work — wear it open and the whole look moves with you.

Ivory cotton shorts embroidered in black folk motifs — diamonds across the leg, a fine border tracing the pockets, the waistband and the hem. Sits high on the waist. Comes as part of a set with the matching cropped top.
A black halter mini cut in glitter-flecked knit, with a deep plunge V and a clean, close line through the body. Layer it over a white tee for daytime, or wear it as it comes after dark.

A black halter mini, sequinned all over so it reads matte until it catches light. Deep plunge neckline, clean through the body, cut above the knee. One piece, one decision, and the evening is handled.
